01 — Visual north star

What this brand must feel like

The brand should feel like: a dimly lit Vietnamese bar on a Friday night — warm pendant lights over dark wood, the smell of broth and cocktails, a group at the bar getting louder. Lived-in, specific, energetic. A place you tell your friends about because it felt like a discovery.

Not like: a Vietnamese restaurant chain with cheerful red placemats, stock photos of pho, and a menu organized for maximum seat turnover. Not polished. Not family-friendly. Not a delivery app landing page.

One-line visual thesis

Street-born Vietnamese energy — warm, moody, and built for a night out.

Anchor adjectives
Warm
Moody

Anti-adjectives

02 — Direction mix

Editorial / Human leads

Editorial / Human — 70% Cutting-edge / Innovative — 30%

The 70% Editorial direction gives Quán Phở its warmth — copy that invites rather than advertises, photography that breathes, hierarchy that feels intentional rather than templated. The 30% Cutting-edge layer keeps it from reading like a neighborhood diner: sharp typographic contrast, bold section pacing, and a dark moody base that signals a night-out destination. An even split would flatten both, making the site feel neither warm nor modern — just competent.

What this mix prevents

  • A food-delivery template aesthetic — thumbnail grids, bright backgrounds, flat UI
  • A heritage-brand look stuck in illustrated menus and serif overuse
  • A nightclub aesthetic where energy drowns the food and warmth
  • A generic "Asian restaurant" visual shorthand — red lanterns, chopstick icons, stock scenery
    03 — Color system

    Dark base. Gold anchor. Crimson once.

    Three layers of near-black build the page's warmth — deep #181008 for the base, surface brown #241810 for cards and sections, and warm mid-brown #5C4232 for section rhythm. Gold #F2B928 is the single interactive color, carrying every CTA and emphasis moment; crimson #C23528 appears exactly once, in the bar promo strip above the footer.

    --core #241810 Surface (cards section fills): Dark warm brown —
    --base-deep #5C4232 Alt section band
    --ink #F0E8D0 Primary text
    --ink-soft #A08060 Text muted: Warm tan —
    --anchor #F2B928 Brand anchor, CTA, dark sections
    --anchor-hover #E0A820 Anchor hover
    --base-wash #F2B92812 Anchor-tinted band
    --accent #C23528 Primary accent
    --accent-deep #A82E22 Accent hover / pressed
    --neon-0 #52E074 Neon signature (logo / brand mark only):

    Usage ratio

    Dark neutrals carry the page. Gold anchors every interactive moment. Crimson appears once — bar promo strip only. Neon green is logo mark only and never enters the UI.

    65% dark neutrals · 20% gold anchor · 10% crimson (bar promo) · logo mark only

    Never do this

  • Use crimson #C23528 as a button color or section header accent outside the bar promo strip
  • Apply the neon green #52E074 anywhere in the UI — it belongs to the logo mark exclusively
  • Place any light or white background on a full-page section
  • Use gold #F2B928 for decorative texture or pattern — it signals interaction and emphasis only
  • Combine gold and crimson in the same section unless that section is the bar promo strip
      • 04 — Typography system

      Be Vietnam Pro leads. Cormorant Garamond accents.

      Be Vietnam Pro carries ~90% of the typographic weight — body copy, navigation, labels, UI sentences, and every CTA. Cormorant Garamond Italic in warm gold appears only at display scale (64px+): once in the hero tagline, and once as a section separator when the page needs an editorial breath. The pairing fits the direction mix — a direct human sans carries the voice, and the display serif adds editorial warmth without tipping into fine-dining territory.

      05 — Layout rhythm

      Flow-based narrative scroll

      The page must pull a first-time visitor from arrival through appetite, trust, and action without ever feeling like a menu website. One uninterrupted dark scroll — no app-style card grids, no paginated navigation, no white sections breaking the mood.

      Section banding sequence

      Nav + Hero
      Full-bleed interior photo + Cormorant Garamond gold tagline + dual CTAs
      Bar promo strip
      1 free spring roll with any bar drink — the only red section on the page
      Menu preview
      3-column card grid: pho, rice plates, Spicy Pho Ti-Ni
      Karaoke night
      Saturday 8PM callout with bar atmosphere photography
      Proof band
      Google star reviews + credential bar + lineage trust line
      Book a Party CTA
      Gold band, centered action button, "Dine in. Order online. Book your party."

      No two adjacent sections may share the same background token — dark-base and dark-core alternate to maintain visual rhythm without needing dividers.

      Grid and spacing

      Max width1200px — content centered; photography can bleed full-widthDesktop columns12-col grid; menu cards use 3-up, proof testimonials use 3-upTablet (≤1024px)Card grid collapses to 2-up; hero stays full-widthMobile (≤768px)All sections 1-col; CTAs stack vertically above the foldSection padding80px top/bottom desktop · 48px mobile (--spacing-section)Grid gutter24px (--grid-gutter)Card radius8px (--border-radius-card) · button radius 6px

      Section patterns used

    • Full-width narrative band — hero, karaoke callout, and atmosphere sections use full-bleed dark photography with text overlay
    • 3-column card grid — menu previews at 3-up desktop, 2-up tablet, 1-up mobile; warm border, no drop shadow
    • Single-color accent band — bar promo strip in crimson, full width, one message, one CTA
    • Proof strip — horizontal row of Google star reviews and credential bar on dark-surface band
    • Gold CTA band — full-width warm-gold background, single centered button, above the footer

        07 — Proof presentation

        Build trust before the order button

        Quán Phở carries medium trust burden — it opened in 2025, has 9 Yelp reviews, and the bar and karaoke are not yet visible on the current website. The proof strategy leads with what exists (real Google reviews, confirmed bar, weekly karaoke) and uses the family lineage as the foundation before asking for a booking or order.

        Phase 1 — now

        Use what exists

        • 3 x 5-star Google reviews — display above the fold on the homepage
        • Yelp 4.0★ with review count in credential bar placement
        • Bar confirmation + Spicy Pho Ti-Ni named explicitly — signals a serious bar program
        • Saturday karaoke at 8PM — specific, repeatable, weekly social proof
        • "Formerly Long's Noodle House — same family, same address" as a trust line below the hero
        Phase 2 — as the brand grows

        Scale with new proof

        • Event photos from karaoke nights — group energy, specific evenings, real faces
        • Party booking testimonials — first groups to use the booking flow
        • Bar program expansion — new cocktails named and featured in the menu card grid
        • Yelp volume growth — update the review count as it rises past 9
        • Press or feature mentions — add when earned, never before

        What must never be fabricated

      • Review scores or counts beyond confirmed Yelp 4.0★ (9 reviews) and the 3 Google homepage reviews
      • Specific seating capacity, pricing tiers, or booking deposit amounts — none confirmed by client
      • Delivery availability, platform name, or delivery zone — not confirmed
      • Awards, press mentions, or "best of" designations — none verified as of this handoff
      • Party booking confirmation flow, capacity messaging, or group pricing — pending client input
          • 08 — Imagery and art direction

          Show the place. Show the drink. Show the night.

          Photography direction

          Bar interiorMoody warm pendant lights, low ambientMedium-wide; bar counter and architecture in frameFood close-upHigh-contrast, studio-lit, clean plates on woodTight frame, single dish; bowl of pho or broken riceCocktailsBacklit, condensation visible, bar context behindClose-to-medium; name the drink — Spicy Pho Ti-NiGroup at barCandid-to-documentary; energy and laughterMedium; bar counter in frame, faces optionalKaraoke nightEvening warm light; stage or mic in shotMedium-wide; people in motion or engaged with mic

          Never use these

        • Stock photography — the confirmed in-house photo library is the only permitted source
        • White or light backgrounds on food shots in-situ — maintain the dark moody aesthetic end-to-end
        • Overhead flat-lay food photography — warm close-ups only, not editorial-shoot styling
        • Generic Vietnamese restaurant interior references — no red-and-gold stock scenery, no stock lantern photos
        • Solo diner shots — Quán Phở is a group and social destination; images should reflect that
        • Studio-white portrait or team photography — use interior context shots instead
        • Parallax or scroll-hijacked hero images — standard CSS background-attachment only
            • 09 — Motion and interaction

            Restrained. Purposeful. Never decorative.

            Motion rules

            Section revealScroll into viewport300ms--ease-softFade-up from 12px below. Not staggered. Not dramatic.Button hoverMouse enter150ms--easeGold dims to #E0A820. No scale transform. No glow.Nav link hoverMouse enter150ms--easeColor shift to --anchor. No underline animation.Card hoverMouse enter150ms--easeBorder opacity lifts slightly. No translateY. No lift shadow.

            What must never animate

          • Hero background image — no parallax, no Ken Burns effect, no scale-on-scroll
          • Text content — no character-by-character reveals, no split or stagger animations on headings
          • Logo mark — no intro spin, pulse, or glow on page load
          • Menu cards on hover — no scale transforms, no 3D flip, no lift shadow
          • Page transitions — no slide or cross-fade between routes; standard browser navigation only
          • Any animation that does not respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

              • Easing curves

              --ease: cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) — UI transitions

              --ease-soft: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) — scroll reveals

              11 — Do / Don't rules

              Blunt. Visual. Operational.

              Do

              • Use existing dark moody interior photography as the visual anchor for every atmospheric section
              • Name the cocktail and dishes specifically in callouts — "Spicy Pho Ti-Ni," not "signature cocktail"
              • Put the gold CTA button above the fold on every major section
              • Show both CTAs (Order Now + Book a Party) in the hero — both are live
              • Use Be Vietnam Pro Bold for all short-sentence copy
              • Keep the bar promo strip (free spring roll) visible early in the page flow
              • Signal Saturday karaoke night with its own dedicated section or callout
              • Use warm gold `#F2B928` for all interactive emphasis — one accent color, consistently applied
              • Allow photography to breathe — generous padding on the dark base
              • Use "formerly Long's Noodle House" lineage as trust copy

              Don't

              • Don't use red as the dominant color on any page — crimson belongs to accent and bar promo strip only
              • Don't add delivery copy until confirmed by client
              • Don't use any stock photography — the existing photo library is the asset
              • Don't use a light or white background on any full-page section
              • Don't introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete system
              • Don't use emojis, fire icons, or "hot items" callouts in the UI
              • Don't use the neon green `#52E074` outside the logo mark
              • Don't use "authentic" as a standalone descriptor — replace with the specific dish or tradition
              • Don't apply parallax effects to the hero image
              • Don't add language switcher without confirmed bilingual content need

              • ## Generator constraints
              • The generator must not:
              • Invent business facts (capacity, pricing, delivery, booking process detail)
              • Introduce random accent colors outside the locked palette
              • Use generic SaaS defaults (blue links, grey buttons, white backgrounds)
              • Contradict the trust-building requirements of a medium-trust-burden new brand
              • Ignore the anti-patterns defined in this handoff
              • Over-stylize beyond the 70% Editorial / Human direction
              • Use the crimson as a primary brand color — it is secondary and accent only
              • Apply neon green (`#52E074`) outside the logo mark
              • Replace Cormorant Garamond with any other display serif

              13 — Implementation notes

              What must be preserved. What can flex.

              Must preserve exactly

            • Hero tagline: Cormorant Garamond Italic, warm gold #F2B928, 64px+ — no font substitutions under any circumstance
            • Gold anchor color #F2B928 and hover state #E0A820 — no tinting, brightness adjustments, or opacity variants in interactive states
            • Bar promo strip background: crimson #C23528 at full opacity — never used as a dominant color anywhere else on the page
            • Neon signature #52E074 — restricted to the logo mark; never in UI, backgrounds, or decorative elements
            • Button uppercase treatment with Be Vietnam Pro Bold 700+ — never sentence case or lowercase for primary and secondary buttons
            • Dark near-black page background #181008 — no light or white sections anywhere on the page
            • Dual CTAs in hero (Order Now + Book a Party) — both visible above the fold simultaneously on desktop

                • Accessibility

              • Gold #F2B928 on dark base #181008 passes 4.5:1 contrast — verify before any shade or opacity adjustment to either color
              • All scroll animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — disable fade-up reveals entirely, not just slow them down
              • Interactive elements (buttons, nav links, menu cards) must show visible :focus-visible outlines at 2px minimum, gold color
              • Both hero CTAs (Order Now and Book a Party) must be keyboard-navigable — tab order must reach both without a pointer
              • All photography must include descriptive alt text: "Interior bar with warm pendant lights and red lanterns" not "bar.jpg"
              • Credential bar text must not rely on color alone — "★ Yelp 4.0" not just colored stars with no label
              • Text overlays on photography (hero tagline, karaoke section copy) must maintain 4.5:1 contrast against the darkest overlay state

                  • Future agents must never improvise

                • Do not introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete locked system; no alternatives, no system fonts in headings
                • Do not add a second section using crimson #C23528 as background — the bar promo strip is the single red-dominant moment on the entire page
                • Do not write delivery copy, capacity figures, or booking process detail without confirmed client input — those decisions are not yet made
                • Do not apply neon green #52E074 to any UI element — it belongs to the logo mark and nowhere else
                • Do not substitute Cormorant Garamond Italic with another display serif for hero tagline moments — the pairing is non-negotiable
